notes: Read all 261 numbered source lines before editing. Native port follows the established dashboard idiom (DriveEfficiencyChartWidget / BatteryHealthAnalyticsWidget): the real native data hooks are imported and every not-yet-ported web dependency (Recharts ComposedChart + chart helpers, WidgetShell, WidgetChartSummary, DataFreshness, useUnits/unitConversion, numberFormat, react-i18next, lucide-react) is reproduced inline native-safe and documented here.

L1 `import { useMemo }` -> native `import {useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useState}` (useCallback stabilises toSpeedDisplay; useEffect/useState drive the inline freshness 30s tick). L2 react-i18next useTranslation('dashboard') -> module-level English-default `t(key, fallback, vars?)` with {{var}} interpolation, keeping every widget.speedProfile.* / freshness.* key verbatim.

L3 lucide-react Activity -> no native icon font: the wide-header icon becomes a small cyan (colors.accent) '\u223F' ActivityGlyph (pulse/activity signal); the WidgetChartSummary emptyIcon Activity (L138/L194) is dropped (native EmptyState has no icon slot), the activity signal preserved by the header glyph.

L4-7 Recharts (ComposedChart/Bar/Line/XAxis/YAxis/Tooltip/ResponsiveContainer) + chart helpers (chartGrid, chartMargin, axisTick, axisTickSm, chartAnimation, fmt) are DOM/SVG-only -> replaced by an inline native `SpeedProfileChart` built from RN Views (same technique as the shared AreaChartWrapper): frequency renders as bars normalised to a left-axis domain (web yAxisId='freq', #6366f1), efficiency renders as dot markers normalised to an independent right-axis domain (web yAxisId='eff', #f59e0b) — preserving the web dual-Y-axis scaling. `fmt` (web charts: fmtNumber at precision, default 1) is inlined verbatim and threaded to the axis formatters exactly as the web YAxis tickFormatter used `${fmt(v,0)}%` (L212) and `fmt(v,0)` (L221).

L8 useSpeedProfile imported unchanged from ../../../api/hooks/useDriving (already-converted native hook; same /analytics/speed-profile path + enabled gating). L9 useVehicles imported unchanged from ../../../api/hooks/useVehicles (vehicles?.[0]?.id fallback preserved). L10 @/hooks/useUnits -> inline `useUnits()` deriving unitPrefs.speed from the native useSettings exactly as web deriveSpeed (unit_of_length === 'mi' -> 'mph' else 'km/h'); only speed is read by this widget so the mirror exposes just that pref (useMemo for reference stability).

L11 @/lib/numberFormat fmtNumber + fmtInt -> inlined verbatim (safeNumber guard, en-US grouping, fmtNumber default precision 2; fmtInt = fmtNumber(v, 0)). L12 './shared' WidgetChartSummary + ChartSummaryStat -> inline `WidgetChartSummary` + local `ChartSummaryStat` (same isEmpty->EmptyState fallback, the same stat row label/value/optional-unit, and the chart rendered below only when !compact, matching web `{!compact && chart}` L61). L13 './WidgetShell' -> inline `WidgetShell`. L14 './types' WidgetProps -> local `WidgetProps`/`WidgetSize` (vehicleId + size.cols read; size.rows kept in the type for parity). L15 @/lib/unitConversion convertSpeedFromSI -> inlined verbatim (km/h = mps*3600/1000, mph = mps*3600/1609.344) with the NIST metre constant + SECONDS_PER_HOUR.

Companion __tests__/SpeedProfileWidgetParity.test.tsx mocks useSpeedProfile (../api/hooks/useDriving), useVehicles and useSettings, and renders: loading skeleton; wide-with-data (Most Common 36-72 / Peak Freq 46.2% / Sweet Spot 0-36 / km/h, chart plot + chart + Frequency/Wh/mi legend + freshness); standard 2x2 (stats + chart); mph units (22-45 bucket, 'mph' not 'km/h'); API optimalSpeedMps sweet spot (25 m/s -> 90); compact (title-less, Most Common + Sweet Spot only, no Peak Freq, no chart plot); empty state ('No speed data'); query-error box ('boom'); and the useSpeedProfile vehicle-id argument (String(firstVehicleId)='7', explicit vehicleId='42', undefined when no vehicle). Every test unmounts so the 30s freshness interval leaves no open handle.

Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint), npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles (jest). No DOM, react-router, framer-motion, lucide-react, Recharts, Leaflet, or old web UI components are imported into the native output.
